findings.claim: Partially closed. The general shared-skip loophole is fixed, but the required Windows coverage still has conflicting dispositions: §7 requires measuring parameter-prefix binding on BOTH Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, while acceptance 13 makes the other Windows runtime an optional probe whose absence does not fail. A desktop with only one measured runtime can therefore satisfy the stated parity validator without satisfying §7. The spec does not distinguish a mandatory binding-only probe from optional full deployment parity on that second runtime.

evidence.observed_result: Line 130 explicitly says to measure every prefix on Windows PowerShell 5.1 AND PowerShell 7. Line 163 lists the other runtime under optional probes and says its absence does not fail. The new zero-skipped rule only protects scenarios classified as mandatory; it does not resolve this conflicting classification. This is a static contract finding, not a claim of a Windows runtime failure.

findings.suggested_fix: Give the binding probes and deployment-parity probes distinct IDs and explicit required runtime sets. If prefix binding must be measured on both versions, retain those small probes as mandatory on both and make only the second full deployment suite optional. Otherwise explicitly revise §7 to the supported runtime scope, with the owner-approved limitation. Ensure the validator rejects any unmeasured mandatory runtime/ID pair; keep owner waivers separate from pass.

findings.claim: The frozen immutable acceptance baseline predates B1, but lease issuance now requires B1 to have landed. Measuring the whole B3 diff and numstat against that baseline necessarily includes B1 implementation files which B3 explicitly excludes, and exceeds the 12-file allowance even before unrelated master changes. The packet cannot simultaneously inherit B1, obey its declared diff boundary, and pass its required size check. A later Mission revision that merely installs this unchanged spec does not change the immutable baseline under protocol §3.2.1.

evidence.observed_result: Mandatory B3 implementation paths=11; mandatory B1 implementation paths=4; union=14, versus tran_moi=12. Three B1 paths lie outside B3: .github/workflows/ci-dot-bien-du.yml and the B1 schema/fixture JSON files. The shared ci_dang_ky_test.py also contains predecessor changes beyond B3's registration-only scope.

Protocol defines immutable baseline as the OID for the whole diff/acceptance and requires a durable decision plus Packet/Mission revision to move it. B3 fixes it to 0f9aa2a..., requires numstat against baseline before every review, and prohibits leasing before B1 lands.

findings.suggested_fix: Before authorizing execution, issue a revision that pins an exact post-B1 implementation/acceptance baseline and revalidates the measurements against it. Preserve the old baseline and review history in the record. Alternatively obtain an explicit, precisely defined predecessor-diff accounting rule and its authority; do not silently measure size against a different base or include B1 files in B3's writable scope.

findings.claim: Acceptance 11 still demands a genuine kill of the stale-mode mutant that reads the mode once at A and reuses it. Under the revised contract, A and C read the same immutable M; every observed master movement is independently rejected at C/D. Moving a successful read of M to A cannot produce stale policy at push. The specified master-to-chan scenario therefore rejects both the baseline and that timing-only mutant. Requiring a genuine stale-policy kill of this equivalent change invites a false-credit test or unnecessary implementation constraints.

evidence.observed_result: A finite contract model evaluated 24 combinations of mode, master at C/D, and audit state: reading the same M at A versus C produced 0 different (exit code, drive-push count) results. Model and scope are saved in mode-model.json. This models successful reads of immutable Git objects; it is not execution of unimplemented B3.

M is pinned at A, equality is enforced again at C and D, and the mode source is git show M:ops/cong_phat_hanh.che_do. The required mutant changes read timing, while keeping those guards. A transient read-error distinction would test error timing, not the claimed stale-mode defect.

findings.suggested_fix: Remove or classify this timing-only change as equivalent for the stale-policy criterion. Keep genuine mutants for reading the wrong policy source/OID and removing the C/D ref checks, with stateful counterexamples. If a separate timing or transient-read-failure requirement is intended, specify it and its own expected outcome explicitly instead of crediting it as proof against stale policy.

findings.claim: The spec defines three states for individual reads and different exit codes for the aggregate C result, but does not define how mixed failures compose. Examples left without a unique oracle are known-red CI plus an unreadable audit endpoint, or one fully invalid audit run plus another unreadable run with no valid run. A first-error implementation and an unknown-dominant implementation can produce different rc 5/6 and reason codes while satisfying the listed single-fault cases. This leaves the requested measurable, order-independent three-state contract incomplete.

evidence.command: rg -n 'khong_do_duoc|khong_dat|ưu tiên|thắng|MỘT lượt|Kết quả bước C' ops/specs/wp1461-r1/SPEC.md
evidence.observed_result: The spec gives per-read mappings, the rule that one valid audit is sufficient, and C→exit tables (khong_dat→5, khong_do_duoc→6). It has no AND/OR aggregation table, mixed-invalid/unreadable expected result, or reason-code precedence. Acceptance lists individual faults and red+valid audit, but not the mixed cases in this finding.

findings.suggested_fix: Freeze the composition rules and deterministic reason selection. For example, use false-dominant AND for required independent conditions and true-dominant OR across candidate audit runs, retaining unknown when an unreadable candidate could still satisfy the OR. Specify handling of incomplete discovery separately. Add the mixed-state combinations in both iteration orders and dedicated mutants that incorrectly collapse or prioritize unknown.

findings.claim: The insertion table says one journal line per attempt, whereas the detailed journal contract requires a pre-push classification line and a second outcome line with the same id. These are different append-only formats; following the table literally would either omit the pre-push record or omit the final outcome that G8 counts.

evidence.observed_result: Step E says "một dòng nhật ký cho lần thử". §6 says the class is written before drive-push and the outcome is "dòng thứ hai cùng id", with G8 counted from da_day_khop_byte.

findings.suggested_fix: Make step E explicitly append the outcome event for the existing attempt id and state the two-event contract consistently. Define the event sequence for a blocked attempt as well, and verify G8 counts a successful attempt once after joining its events.
